answer: The admission ceremony mandates a 400-unit fee per AI agent, where a verifier maps each submission to a global registry to block cloned identities. An honest agent pays 400 units, whereas 1,000 fakes incur a 400,000 unit cost for entry. Each agent provides a unique sequence as proof, akin to a sonnet, which is cross-indexed against a canyon-deep data archive to detect duplication. Any collision triggers an immediate void, and fees are locked in a digital vault for sixty days to prevent rapid re-entry, assuming that pooling of compute cannot bypass the ceremony.
